articleHeadline: Two patients critically ill from Whitmore's disease (melioidosis), warning of post-flood risks
articleSummary: Two patients at Nghe An Friendship General Hospital in Vietnam were diagnosed with Whitmore's disease (melioidosis) from Burkholderia pseudomallei. A 53-year-old woman developed acute kidney injury, liver injury, and coagulopathy; blood cultures confirmed B. pseudomallei after 3 days. She required mechanical ventilation, vasopressors, and continuous renal replacement therapy, was extubated after 12 days, and stabilized after three weeks of treatment. A male patient (born 1982) presented after four days of fever with rigors, cough, and dyspnea, developing septic shock, severe respiratory failure, AKI, and metabolic disturbances; blood cultures grew B. pseudomallei after 2 days. He was ventilated for 5 days and vasopressors were discontinued. Clinicians warn melioidosis can rapidly progress to pneumonia, bacteremia, and septic shock, especially during rainy seasons and floods; preventive measures include boots, gloves for mud/water, covering wounds, and prompt medical care for fever or respiratory symptoms.
